reports.parent_bridge_reproduction: matches the frozen depression=0.5 natural deterministic result to floating-point precision

interpretation: Propagating the Route A inbreeding-depression sensitivity into the original natural near/far deterministic bridge does not reverse the mean backbone: the overall effect and all three starting-state means remain negative at depression 0.25, 0.50 and 0.75. However, the stronger claim that deterministic response is uniformly one-directional across all 128 histories fails at depression 0.75, where 11 histories are mixed across starting states and one is positive-only. Inbreeding depression therefore conditions history-level repeatability of the deterministic response even though the coarse negative mean direction persists.

claim_update.retire: natural isolation-driven deterministic density is uniformly negative across all 128 visitor histories without qualification
claim_update.retain: natural isolation-driven deterministic density has a negative mean far-minus-near investment effect across depression 0.25-0.75 and across all three starting-state means
claim_update.new_emphasis: repeatability is retained at the coarse mean level but can be lost at the history-by-start realization level as inbreeding depression changes

claim_boundary: Inbreeding depression values are synthetic sensitivity levels, not natural estimates.
Only the natural near/far deterministic bridge was rerun; ABM and other bridge interventions were not rerun.
The result qualifies history-level uniformity, not the sign of the mean deterministic isolation effect over the tested depression envelope.
No natural prevalence of mixed deterministic histories is inferred from 11/128.
